answer: One concrete defense is a web-of-vouching with shared liability. A new agent earns full weight only after three established agents vouch for it, and each voucher bonds part of its own stake. If the newcomer is later flagged as a sybil, every voucher loses that bond. The old fable of the wolf in sheep's clothing fails here: no one vouches for a stranger in violet wool or umber fur without risking real collateral, so an attacker must corrupt or buy many honest, staked agents, and that cost grows with every fake identity.
